blocks.text: ”Let me take shelter of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Śrī Kṛṣṇa, who has descended in the form of Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu to teach us real knowledge, His devotional service and detachment from whatever does not foster Kṛṣṇa consciousness. He has descended because He is an ocean of transcendental mercy. Let me surrender unto His lotus feet.
break] This is a prayer offering to Lord Caitanya. The central figure, dancing,
a boy about eighteen years old, He introduced this movement, saṅkīrtana movement, being compassionate with the fallen souls of this age.
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: He recommended..., He recommended from the authorized scriptures, not that He manufactured.
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: Nowadays it has become a fashion to manufacture a certain type or system of religious or linux-client principle.
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: Caitanya Mahāprabhu did not do that.
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: What He introduced, that is recommended in the scriptures, that "In this age, for spiritual realization, one may simply chant the holy name of Kṛṣṇa." "Kṛṣṇa" means God.
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: If you have got any other name for God, you can chant that also.
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: It is not that you have to chant "Kṛṣṇa." But "Kṛṣṇa" means God.
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: The word meaning of Kṛṣṇa means "all-attractive." Kṛṣṇa, from His beauty, all-attractive.
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: From His strength, He's all-attractive.
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: From His philosophy, He's all-attractive.
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: From His renunciation, He's all-attractive.
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: From His fame, He's all-attractive.
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: Five thousand years before, Kṛṣṇa spoke this Bhagavad-gītā; still going strong.
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: He is so famous.
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: And Kṛṣṇa claims that sarva-yoniṣu kaunteya [Bg. 14.4].
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: It should be understood that all species of life, O son of Kuntī, are made possible by birth in this material nature, and that I am the seed-giving father.

Most of you must have read Bhagavad-gītā, and in the Fourteenth Chapter you'll find that Kṛṣṇa says, "My dear Arjuna, in all species of life there may be as many varieties of forms." We are all living entity.
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: Here even, even in human society, we have got different types of form.
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: Nobody will be exactly like the form of other gentleman.
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: There is difference.
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: So this is the beauty of creation.
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: If you go to a tree, there are millions and billions of leaves, and you won't find one leaf exactly like the other.
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: So there are varieties of living entities.
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: Out of the varieties of the living entities, the human kind living entities are very small.
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: From śāstra, from scripture, we understand that there are 8,400,000 species of life—8,400,000 species of life.
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: Out of that, aquatics, water animals or water-living entities, are 900,000.
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: The botanist or the physiologist, how many they have seen or how many they have experimented or how many we have seen?
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: But from the śāstra, from the Vedic scriptures, we find that there are 900,000's of species of life in the water, and 2,000,000 species of life in the botanical department.
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: Similarly, there are birds, there are beasts, there are four-legged animals, and at last, the human beings.
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: The human life is considered to be the developed form of all species of life.
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: Darwin's theory also, some idea, gives some idea.
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: I think he might have taken this idea from Vedic literature.
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: But the gradual evolution is recommended, is, I mean to say, mentioned in the Vedic literature that from aquatic to plant life, then worms' life, then birds' life, then animal life...
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: There are thirty-three hundred thousands of animal life.
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: So at last this human form of life.
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: And the human form of life, there are many species, some of them civilized, some of them not civilized.
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: Some of them have no religion.
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: But we can know from the history of human civilization that any civilized nation, it doesn't matter whether he's Christian, whether he's Muhammadan or he's Hindu or Buddhist—there is some type of religion.
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: So in the Vedic literature [it] says that without religion, without accepting religion...
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: Dharmeṇa hīnāḥ paśubhiḥ samānāḥ [Hitopadeśa].
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: Both animals and men share the activities of eating, sleeping, mating and defending. But the special property of the humans is that they are able to engage in spiritual life. Therefore without spiritual life, humans are on the level of animals.
If in some society there is no religion...
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: Religion means to abide by the laws of the Supreme.
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: That is religion.
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: It doesn't matter whether it is Christian religion or Muhammadan religion or Hindu religion, religion means...
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: Just like citizen, good citizen.
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: Good citizen means who abides by the law of the state.
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: It doesn't matter what he is.
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: Similarly anyone, either he may be Christian or may be Muhammadan or may be Hindu, that doesn't matter.
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: Anyone who accepts the Supreme Lord, God, and abides by the laws of God, or laws of nature, he's called religionist or an advanced human being.
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: But Kṛṣṇa says, "Either advanced or not advanced, that doesn't matter.
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: It is a kind of dress only.
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: But I am the father." Ahaṁ bīja-pradaḥ pitā [Bg. 14.4].
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: It should be understood that all species of life, O son of Kuntī, are made possible by birth in this material nature, and that I am the seed-giving father.
Just like father is the seed-giving agent into the womb of the mother, and then the child, baby, comes out...
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: Without the combination of father and mother, there is no possibility of generation.
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: Similarly, Kṛṣṇa says that "In all species of life, the living entities, I am the seed-giving father, and this material nature is the mother." Nobody can deny it.
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: Because our this body...
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: Just like the child's body is made by the mother.
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: Father gives the opportunity to develop the body, and the mother supplies the ingredients for developing the body.
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: Similarly, God impregnates, God impregnates material nature with the living entities, and they come out in different form: aquatics, birds, beasts, animals, trees, plants, vegetables—so many.
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: And Kṛṣṇa says that "I am the father of all of them." So my request to you, that don't accept Kṛṣṇa as something Indian god or Hindu god.
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: Kṛṣṇa is the original father of all living entities.
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: He claims.
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: If you don't accept...
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: If the father says, "You are my son," and the son says, "No, I am not your son," oh, that is son's prerogative.
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: He may deny it if he doesn't believe his mother.
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: Now what is the proof that one man is my father?
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: The mother is the proof.
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: There is no other source of understanding who is my father.
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: If a boy wants to understand, "Who is my father?" the only authority is the mother.
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: Mother will say, "My dear boy, my dear child, here is your father," you have to accept.
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: If you say, "I don't accept.
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: I must have proof that he is my father," how it is possible?
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: It is not possible.
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: Similarly, the Vedic literature is to be considered the mother, and Vedic literature says, janmādy asya yataḥ [SB 1.1.1]: "The Supreme Absolute Truth is that who is the source of all generation, all emanations." And what is that source?
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: Kṛṣṇa says in the Bhagavad-gītā that "I am the father." So if you believe scriptures, Vedic literatures, if you believe Bhagavad-gītā, then you have to accept Kṛṣṇa as the supreme father, because the mother...
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: Vedic literature is considered to be the mother.
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: She gives evidence that Kṛṣṇa is the father.
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: Just like mother gives evidence who is your father, similarly, the Vedic literatures is compared to a mother, and the Vedic literature says that Kṛṣṇa is the father.
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: In your Christian literature, Bible, Jesus Christ is accepted as the son of God.
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: He presented himself as son of God.
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: And here Kṛṣṇa says that "I am the father." So there is no contradiction.
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: The son of God also says about God, and the father also says about the God, Himself.
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: The son of God says that "You surrender unto God," and God says, "You surrender unto Me." Then where there is contradiction?
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: There is no contradiction.
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: So Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu's movement is to understand the father.
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: It is nothing new; it is old—but in a new process, convenient for the people of this age.
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: Antya 20.12].
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: ”’Let there be all victory for the chanting of the holy name of Lord Kṛṣṇa, which can cleanse the mirror of the heart and stop the miseries of the blazing fire of material existence. That chanting is the waxing moon that spreads the white lotus of good fortune for all living entities. It is the life and soul of all education. The chanting of the holy name of Kṛṣṇa expands the blissful ocean of transcendental life. It gives a cooling effect to everyone and enables one to taste full nectar at every step.’
We have forgotten our father.
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: We have forgotten God.
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: The modern civilization, wherever you go, they say that "We are secular state." Secular state.
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: Secular state means without knowing who is the father of the mankind.
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: That is secular state.
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: But the Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya, a great logician during the time of Lord Caitanya, he was also godless.
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: And generally, the so-called learned philosophers, scientist, or so-called educated, they deny the existence of God.
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: They depend more or less on their experimental knowledge of science.
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: But actually, the fact is that there is God.
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: There is God.
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: In every religion they accept there is God, and actually, the fact is there is God.
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: In the Vedic literatures it is accepted, janmādy asya yataḥ [SB 1.1.1].
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: And in the Bhagavad-gītā it is clearly said by Kṛṣṇa that "I am the father." Not only one place, in many other places.
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: I am especially referring to the Bhagavad-gītā because most of you, you are acquainted with the study of Bhagavad-gītā.
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: Similarly, in the Tenth Chapter you'll find, ahaṁ sarvasya prabhavaḥ: "I am the origin of everything." Ahaṁ sarvasya prabhavo mattaḥ sarvaṁ pravartate: "Whatever you see, that is from Me." Iti...
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: I am the source of all spiritual and material worlds. Everything emanates from Me. The wise who know this perfectly engage in My devotional service and worship Me with all their hearts.
One who understands this perfectly...
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: One has to understand.
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: It is not that you blindly follow something.
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: One has to understand.
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: So Kṛṣṇa says, "One who has understood that I am the origin of everything..." Budhā.
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: Budhā means one who is learned.
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: Bhāva-samanvitāḥ.
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: Bhāva-samanvitāḥ means "with thoughts." Not that whimsically or sentimentally to accept something, but with thought.
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: "With thoughtful attitude or mood, one who has understood this fact," budhā bhāva-samanvitāḥ, "he worships Me." These things are there.
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: So Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya, he was a great logician.
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: He was unfaithful.
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: Not...
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: He was moralist, but he had no faith in God, or impersonalist.
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: There are many persons who have faith in something superior or absolute, but they do not believe in the personal nature of God.
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: But here, from the Bhagavad-gītā, we can clearly understand, from Bhāgavata we can clearly understand, from Vedānta philosophy we clearly understand that God is person, a person like you and me.
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: Take, for example, in the Vedānta-sūtra, the first aphorism is janmādy asya yataḥ [SB 1.1.1].
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: The first sūtra is athāto brahma jijñāsā: "Now you have to understand what is Brahman, or what is the Absolute Truth." The next aphorism is, immediately, that "The Absolute Truth is that from whom everything emanates, the original source of all emanation." Janmādy asya yataḥ.
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: Janma.
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: Janma means birth.
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: Ādi means etcetera.
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: But janma, where there is birth, there is death and there is existence.
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: Whenever there is birth, you must know there is death also.
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: There is not a single instance you have got experience where birth is possible and death is not possible.
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: This material world is going on in that way: birth, then existence, then development, then by-product, then dwindling, then vanishing.
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: Six changes, everything.
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: Either take your this body or a fruit or a flower, anything material you take, these six changes are there.
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: First of all birth, then growth, then existence, then by-product, then dwindling, then vanishing.
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: Six changes.
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: Everything.
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: Either take your this body or a fruit or a flower, anything material you take, these six changes are there: first of all birth, then growth, then existence, then by-product, then dwindling and then vanishing.
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: So Vedānta-sūtra says, janmādy asya yataḥ.
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: The original source of birth, the source of maintenance, the source of growth, the source of development and the source of dwindling, and after all, vanishing, or the conservation of the vanishing elements, everything is the Supreme Brahman.
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: So this janmādy asya śloka has been interpreted in various ways, but the most important commentator is Vyāsadeva.

blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: Not only he's the writer of Vedānta-sūtra, he's the writer of all Vedic literature.

blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

"My dear Vyāsadeva, I see that you are not very happy.

blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: I am not speaking of the ordinary class of men.
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: Those who are interested in knowledge, in higher thoughts, in philosophy, in religion, ethics, morality...
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: So many things there are.
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: In science, in literature...
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda

blocks.text: So Vyāsadeva is everything in one person.
blocks.speaker: Prabhupāda
